segments.text: 90% of consumers use Google Business Profile to find local businesses.
segments.narration: 90 percent of consumers use Google Business Profile to find local businesses.

You’re pouring money into a website, hoping it’ll magically bring in a flood of new customers. But the phone isn’t ringing, and the leads aren’t flowing. Many small business owners feel stuck in this frustrating cycle - spending on marketing without seeing a return.

It’s like having a store with no sign - people simply won’t find you. Your Google Business Profile (GBP) is your free storefront. Most small businesses set it up, then neglect it. You need to treat it like a vital part of your marketing.

A study by Trustpilot found that 92 percent of consumers trust online reviews as much as personal recommendations. Google wants to know exactly who you are. Your name, address, and phone number (NAP) must match exactly everywhere online - your website, Google Maps, Yelp, Facebook, and any other directory.

This is your most powerful, free marketing tool. Here’s how to do it right: 1. Verify Your Listing: Go to Google Business Profile and verify your business. It’s a quick process that’ll unlock more features. Complete Your Profile: Fill out every section.

Google needs to know exactly who you are and where you are. Stop waiting for customers to tell you what you do. Start asking happy clients for a quick review after a good job. That feedback is what local searchers look for.

If your website doesn’t get calls, it’s not working for your business. Your Google Business Profile is your free storefront. Set up your hours, services, and photos right. If you miss anything here, you’re leaving money on the table. Stop waiting for customers to tell you what you do.

Tell people exactly what you fix or what you do. If you build something fancy that nobody calls, it isn't working for your business. Your Google Business Profile is your free storefront. Set up your hours, services, and photos right now. This is where local people find you.
